title: bug: JetBrains protected selection treats a subst or mapped drive letter that names the project as outside it
description:
Objective: under the protected profile on Windows, JetBrains must not keep a PATH entry, or accept a node or installed candidate, whose drive letter is a subst or mapped-network alias of the project (or of a folder holding it). Found on 2026-10-30 by architect-4ae016fb while planning task-526a208079b5467db13cb9dd10da442e (the UNC/device refusal).

Evidence (native Windows, Temurin JDK 17.0.20, node v24.16.0; probe scripts in D:\arch-526a-probe\, outside the repo):
- `subst Q: <dir>\project`, then PATH=`Q:\bin`: a bare-name spawnSync from an outside cwd ran the project's copy of whoami.exe (spawn.cjs).
- Java `Paths.get("Q:\\bin").toRealPath()` returns `Q:\bin` (Subst.java). WindowsLinkSupport.getRealPath walks components with FindFirstFile and calls GetFinalPathNameByHandle only at a reparse point, so a subst drive letter is never resolved.
- So RuntimeSelectionPolicy.isOutsideProject finds no project prefix in either form and answers true, and MoeDaemonSupervisor.protectedPathEntries keeps the entry. select/installedExecutable would accept a node under such a drive the same way.
- A mapped network drive (`net use Z: \\localhost\C$\...`) takes the same Java code path (no reparse point, so the drive spelling is kept). Not probed.
- `Files.isSameFile(Paths.get("Q:\\bin"), <project>\bin)` is true, and so are the `\\.\Volume{...}` and `\\localhost\D$` spellings. File identity (volume serial + file index) sees through every alias.
- VS Code is not affected: Node's fs.realpathSync.native (GetFinalPathNameByHandle) returns `D:\...\project\bin` for `Q:\bin` (subst-node.cjs), so its isOutsideProject finds the project.
- task-526a2080 refuses only Windows forms that are not drive-qualified. `Q:\` is drive-qualified, so that rule does not catch this.

Deliverable: on a Windows host, RuntimeSelectionPolicy proves a drive-qualified candidate (a PATH entry, or the real path select accepts) outside the project by file identity as well as by spelling.
- Suggested mechanism: refuse when the real path, or any ancestor of it, is Files.isSameFile with the project's real root.
- Alternative: refuse drive letters that are not plain local volumes.
The architect picks the mechanism. It must:
- fail closed: an identity lookup that fails answers not-outside;
- never contact a share (UNC and device forms are already refused first, by task-526a2080);
- keep the per-PATH-entry cost bounded.
Accepted cost, if the drive-type route is taken: a PATH entry or node under a subst or mapped drive is not used under the protected profile.

Not in scope:
- UNC and device forms (task-526a2080);
- VS Code (unaffected);
- trailing-dot spellings (toRealPath normalizes them);
- persistent state;
- enabling verified-local.
Local drive paths that are not aliases, POSIX hosts and the legacy profile do not change.

Depends on task-526a208079b5467db13cb9dd10da442e, which edits the same RuntimeSelectionPolicy.kt and RuntimeSelectionPolicyTest.kt.

Verification command: cd moe-jetbrains && ./gradlew test. WSL has no JDK, so run cmd.exe /d /c "set GRADLE_OPTS=-Xmx512m&& cd /d D:\projexts\moes\moe-jetbrains && .\gradlew.bat test --rerun" under the jetbrains-gradle lease. It must exit 0.
definitionOfDone: On a Windows host, RuntimeSelectionPolicy.isOutsideProject returns false for a subst drive spelling of the project and of a folder inside it. It also returns false when the drive is substed to the project's parent and the entry reaches the project (Q:\<project name>\bin). The protected daemon PATH drops such entries but keeps an unrelated folder on the same subst drive. Shown by new JetBrains unit tests. They create a temporary subst drive on a free letter, always remove it in a finally block, and skip only when no letter is free.
On a Windows host, a node candidate under such a drive is refused with a named reason and no daemon is spawned. Shown by tests.
Drive paths that are not aliases, POSIX hosts and the legacy profile behave as before: the existing RuntimeSelectionPolicyTest and MoeDaemonSupervisorTest cases pass unchanged.

cd moe-jetbrains && ./gradlew test exits 0 (from WSL: cmd.exe /d /c "set GRADLE_OPTS=-Xmx512m&& cd /d D:\projexts\moes\moe-jetbrains && .\gradlew.bat test --rerun"), with output supplied to complete_task.

Do not enable verified-local or claim isolation until all requisite implementation and certification gates pass.

implementationPlan.description:
Add a bounded Windows DOS-drive expansion helper using the JNA already in IntelliJ, plus its injected tests. No new dependency or process-based production lookup. Verified SDK util-8.jar contains com.sun.jna.platform.win32.Kernel32 and com.intellij.jna.JnaLoader; Kernel32.QueryDosDevice(String, char[], int) is present. Do not add GetFinalPathNameByHandle or GetDriveType: neither is needed to recover a subst target, and a drive-type/filesystem probe is not a safe substitute for the no-share boundary.

In RuntimeSelectionPolicy add these internal seams (new symbols):
  @Volatile internal var windowsDriveTarget: (String) -> String? = ::queryWindowsDriveTarget
  internal fun resolveWindowsDrivePath(path: String, query: (String) -> String? = windowsDriveTarget): String?
Error handling is fail-closed throughout. The native provider is lazy in use, checks JnaLoader.isLoaded(), then calls Kernel32.INSTANCE.QueryDosDevice("X:", CharArray(32768), 32768). Read ONLY the first NUL-terminated mapping within the returned count; Microsoft documents later strings as historical mappings. Zero, missing terminator, empty/current malformed value, count outside the buffer, unavailable JNA, Exception, IOError or LinkageError return null. Never retry indefinitely, enumerate all drives, shell out, or cache mappings across calls. resetForTest restores the native provider without initializing JNA.

resolveWindowsDrivePath is string-only and testable on POSIX. Accept a drive-qualified input spelling, preserve the path suffix, and repeatedly expand a current mapping of the exact form "\??\X:\absolute\target" by prepending that target to the suffix. Normalize separator spelling only; do not interpret a remote/device target as a DOS path. Reject cycles by case-insensitive drive letter, more than 26 queries, or expanded paths over 32767 UTF-16 units. A terminal mapping must be an entire recognized local device root (case-insensitive), never a prefix: \Device\HarddiskVolume<digits>, \Device\CdRom<digits>, \Device\Floppy<digits>, or \Device\Ramdisk with an optional numeric suffix. Return the expanded DOS spelling, NOT the NT device spelling. Reject UNC, \??\UNC, Mup, LanmanRedirector/WebDAV, unknown device families, root-plus-directory NT targets, malformed values and lookup failures. Unknown device mappings are unprovable and fail closed; do not infer "local" from any arbitrary \Device prefix. Existing normal disk/removable-volume paths stay unchanged; exotic third-party mappings are unsupported unless positively recognized (record this limitation for RF07).

Table-test the helper with fake query maps, no network: direct physical drive; subst to project/bin; parent subst plus unrelated sibling; two chained drives; lower-case letters; a current remote mapping followed by an old local mapping; cycles/self-cycle; missing/throwing/LinkageError provider; overlong expansion; UNC/remote/unknown and HarddiskVolume1\directory targets. Assert exact expanded spelling or null and query-count bounds; no native lookup on the fake path. Native provider smoke is exercised by the Windows subst regressions, not replaced by a fake.

The plain JUnit task removes IntelliJPlatformArgumentProvider, so test-native dispatch needs explicit SDK setup. In build.gradle.kts's existing test.doFirst, on Windows only, derive the SDK lib directory from the test classpath's util-8.jar and set jna.boot.library.path to its existing jna/amd64 (x86_64/amd64) or jna/aarch64 (aarch64/arm64) directory. Require jnidispatch.dll to exist; fail with a clear Gradle setup error rather than letting every protected test silently refuse. Preserve the existing JVM-argument filtering. Do not hard-code this workstation's C:\Users path, change production search paths, or add native settings on Linux/macOS.
implementationPlan.note:
RuntimeSelectionPolicy: new internal seams `@Volatile windowsDriveTarget: (String) -> String? = ::queryWindowsDriveTarget`, `resolveWindowsDrivePath(path, query = windowsDriveTarget)` and `currentDosMapping(buffer, count)`. resolveWindowsDrivePath is string-only: separators -> '\', requires ^[A-Za-z]:\, expands `\??\X:\folder` targets (DOS_TARGET: segments non-empty, not ending '.'/' ', no reserved chars) by prefixing the target to the suffix, stops at a whole recognized local device (\Device\HarddiskVolume<n>|CdRom<n>|Floppy<n>|Ramdisk[n], case-insensitive, entire string) and returns the expanded DOS spelling. Null for non-drive spellings, remote/UNC/Mup/Lanman/WebDAV/unknown/root+dir/malformed mappings, a repeated letter (cycle; so <= 26 queries), > 32767 chars, or a throwing provider (Exception/IOError/LinkageError). Native provider: JnaLoader.isLoaded() then Kernel32.INSTANCE.QueryDosDevice(drive, CharArray(32768), 32768); currentDosMapping reads only the first NUL-terminated string within count (0/negative/over-buffer/no terminator/empty -> null). No caching, no process, no enumeration. resetForTest restores the provider (function reference only, no JNA init).
build.gradle.kts test.doFirst (Windows only, after the existing JVM-arg filtering): arch amd64/x86_64 -> amd64, aarch64/arm64 -> aarch64, util-8.jar located on the test classpath, jna.boot.library.path = <sdk lib>/jna/<arch>; missing jar/dll/arch -> clear Gradle error. No hard-coded user paths; nothing on Linux/macOS.
Test N10 (runs on POSIX too): expansions (physical, CdRom/Floppy/Ramdisk, subst to project/bin, parent subst + sibling, two-drive chain asking [Y:,W:,C:], lower-case letters, root target), zero queries for non-drive/overlong inputs, 16 refused mappings, missing mapping, 2-cycle [A:,B:], self-cycle [S:], 26-drive cycle = exactly 26 queries, throwing/UnsatisfiedLinkError/IOError providers, currentDosMapping rows incl. remote-current + local-history -> null, and a Windows native smoke (SystemRoot expands to itself through the SDK JNA).
GREEN: cmd.exe /d /c "set GRADLE_OPTS=-Xmx512m&& cd /d D:\projexts\moes\moe-jetbrains && .\gradlew.bat test --tests com.moe.util.RuntimeSelectionPolicyTest.N10* --rerun" -> exit 0, 1 test 0 failures. Scratch mutants (files restored, cmp-verified): any-\Device-prefix-local, last-string history, no cycle guard, no jna.boot.library.path -> each exit 1 with the expected N10 assertion. Integration (step 3) not yet wired; N9 still RED by design. Lease released.

implementationPlan.description:
Integrate the drive proof without changing public signatures, accepted File/PATH spellings, or LEGACY behavior. All new native work is gated by profile == RuntimeProfile.PROTECTED && windowsHost. The strict-default public overloads and explicit internal RuntimeProfile overloads remain.

Preflight a drive-qualified candidate/root before the existing toRealPath or Files reads in isOutsideProject, installedExecutable and installedArtifact. For a native mapping that is remote/unknown/unavailable, isOutsideProject returns false; selection refuses with the existing "$label is not a plain local Windows path" reason. Null installed roots and blank/relative/malformed executable paths keep their existing reasons. Also preflight a drive-qualified project before realPathOrNull(basePath), so the identity proof does not open a mapped share. Unprovable project resolution keeps "the project directory cannot be resolved"; the sibling 52fb6178 owns BASE_NOT_PLAIN and its full raw/non-plain-base policy. This task must not add that sibling's trailing-dot/base UI rules. Keep existing UNC/device spelling refusal; do not resolve a remote drive target to inspect it. For real paths discovered after NIO, recheck the drive mapping before any further identity/file checks. Do not make the injected resolve callback run on a preflight refusal.

Replace outsideByIdentity's truncated ancestor input with expanded physical ancestors. Expand both project and candidate, not just candidate (N8's reverse case matters). Resolve existing expanded paths with toRealPath before walking their parents; a subst target can itself contain a junction. A small private helper for existing paths may repeat drive expansion -> toRealPath until expansion no longer changes the resolved path, with a visited set and a 26-round cap; any cycle/overflow/error fails closed. The project must resolve. During the candidate walk, NoSuchFileException advances to the parent of the expanded missing spelling, preserving usableStore roots whose leaf/parents do not exist yet; other errors refuse. Once an existing path resolves, compare Files.isSameFile against the expanded real project and continue from that resolved path's parent, NOT from the old alias parent's spelling. True requires at least one successful identity check and no project match. Never convert an unresolved/missing project into an outside answer. Keep identity in addition to all current lexical/root-containment checks.

Use expanded spellings only for proof: successful installedExecutable/installedArtifact still return the same real File as before, and protected PATH keeps the validated original outside spelling. Do not reinterpret ".." relative to the expanded target: retain the original OS real-path resolution before proving an existing candidate, and normalize missing candidate paths in their original drive coordinate system as today.

Add integration error-handling tests with windowsDriveTarget replaced/restored in try/finally: remote mapping and native failure refuse before a throwing candidate resolve callback, and node/artifact refuse without a fake spawn. Unknown lookup never falls back to the old ancestor walk. LEGACY with a throwing native provider still preserves installed stop selection/PATH; on POSIX the provider must not be called. Retain the old N5-N8/S7-S9 and supervisor W31-W35 controls unchanged. Add concise KDoc explaining hidden drive-root ancestors, why device mappings are queried before NIO, the bounded algorithm and unsupported unknown device families. No docs sweep here; include the runtime/JNA and unusual-device limitations in the RF07 handoff. No changes to profile persistence/projectKey, supervisor, state-store implementation, VM/launcher or VS Code; verified-local stays unavailable.
implementationPlan.note:
Drive proof integrated (PROTECTED && windowsHost only, via strict(profile)); public signatures, accepted File/PATH spellings and LEGACY unchanged.
- unprovableDrive(path): a drive-qualified spelling whose QueryDosDevice chain is not a local volume. Asked BEFORE NIO for the isOutsideProject candidate + project, the installedExecutable candidate ("node executable is not a plain local Windows path"), the installedArtifact root ("installed <rel> is not a plain local Windows path", after the null-root reason) and the select project ("the project directory cannot be resolved"). Rechecked on select's real path before Files.isRegularFile. isOutsideProject's injected resolve never runs on a preflight refusal.
- physicalPath(real): expand -> realPathOrNull until expanding changes nothing; visited set + 26-round cap; any failure null.
- physicalProject: drive project -> physicalPath; non-drive (UNC) real project kept as it resolved (52fb6178 owns BASE_NOT_PLAIN; no base rules added).
- outsideByIdentity(path, physicalProject?): expands path (original real path, or normalized missing spelling in its own drive coordinates), walks NoSuchFile parents of the EXPANDED spelling to the nearest existing folder, toRealPath + physicalPath it, then isSameFile against the physical project from that resolved path up (never alias parents). True needs >=1 comparison and no match; null project/unprovable/other error = false.
- queryWindowsDriveTarget's own catch dropped: resolveWindowsDrivePath (its only caller) already catches Exception/IOError/LinkageError from any provider. build.gradle.kts JNA lookup compacted 5->2 lines (still fails loudly), only for the size budget.
Tests: N11 (Windows; remote/ImDisk0/UnsatisfiedLinkError providers + one remote letter: false before a throwing resolve, node/artifact/project reasons, supervisor starts nothing; native controls accept), N12 (all hosts; throwing provider never asked by LEGACY stop/PATH, nor PROTECTED off Windows). withDriveTargets swaps/restores in try/finally. Old N5-N8/S7-S9/W31-W35 untouched.

implementationPlan.note:
Adversarial self-review of this task's diff (the three paths only; peers' dirty files untouched). Answers to the step-5 questions:

1. Can a descendant subst root or a junction under its target hide the project's parents? No. outsideByIdentity expands the letter (resolveWindowsDrivePath), resolves the nearest existing folder with toRealPath (junctions), re-expands it (physicalPath), then walks the physical parents by isSameFile.
   - Evidence: N9 (descendant root and junction root; `$d\` and `$d\missing\leaf` inside) and QA's probe descendant-root shape.

2. Can a project opened through subst bypass the reverse check? No. physicalProject expands the project.
   - FOUND A GAP and fixed it with a test only: nothing exercised select() with a subst-opened project. N8:525 covers isOutsideProject, but false there cannot tell "proved inside" from "refused as unprovable".
   - Added a 5-line reverse block to N9 (new this round; existing cases unchanged): subst of the project's parent; the node in <project>\bin with basePath "$d\proj" → "node executable resolves inside the project"; the outside node with the same basePath → Accepted(realFile(node)).
   - MUTANT (physicalPath returns null instead of following an expansion) → RuntimeSelectionPolicyTest 60 run, 1 failed: only N9, ComparisonFailure "expected:<node executable resolves inside the project> but was:<the project directory cannot be resolved>". Every other test passed under the mutant.
   - Source restored byte-identical (cmp against the backup).

3. Does an unknown or remote mapping, or a failed native load, lead to any NIO lookup or fallback acceptance? No. unprovableDrive preflights the candidate, root and project before NIO, and `real` is rechecked after NIO.
   - Evidence: N11 covers 3 providers (LanmanRedirector, ImDisk, UnsatisfiedLinkError). Its `untouched` resolver throws AssertionError on any lookup, and the refusal messages are specific.

4. Are historical MULTI_SZ entries ignored? Yes. currentDosMapping takes only the first string, which must be NUL-terminated within the count. N10 covers a remote-first history.

5. Are cycles, length and native errors bounded?
   - Each letter is queried at most once (26 maximum). Paths are capped at 32767 chars and the buffer at 32768.
   - Exception, IOError and LinkageError lead to refusal.
   - physicalPath runs at most 26 rounds over a seen-set.
   - Evidence: N10.

6. Are missing store leaves still supported? Yes. Missing folders defer to their parent. Evidence: the N9 control `newStore().usableFor` with a missing root.

7. Can native initialization run under LEGACY or POSIX? No. Every native path is behind strict(profile) = PROTECTED && windowsHost. Evidence: N12 makes no queries (LEGACY on Windows; every profile elsewhere) and its stop/PATH positives still pass.
   - I re-read the supervisor to confirm N12's PROTECTED branch holds on POSIX CI: isPlainLocalPath is true off Windows, and the stop command uses real paths.

8. Are provider state and owned mappings cleaned up on every failure? Yes. withDriveTargets restores in finally, and resetForTest resets the provider. withSubst removes only the letter it created, in finally, and a body failure keeps its own error. `subst` printed nothing after every run.

implementationPlan.description:
Windows: prove a drive-qualified candidate outside the project by file identity. Production change, one file: moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/util/RuntimeSelectionPolicy.kt.

Start by re-reading the file as task-526a2080 landed it. That task is the dependency; its plan adds `windowsHost`, `isPlainLocalPath(path, windows)`, isOutsideProject's trailing `resolve` seam with the spelling checked first, and select's first plain-local branch. Adapt the names below if it landed differently.

(a) Add a private helper `outsideByIdentity(path: Path, project: Path): Boolean`. It walks `current = path`, then `current.parent`, up to the root, and calls `Files.isSameFile(current, project)` on each:
- isSameFile compares volume serial + file index and follows links.
- If any call answers true, return false: the path is the project or inside it.
- Skip a NoSuchFileException: a missing folder holds nothing, and its parent decides.
- Error handling fails closed: any other exception returns false.
- Return true only if at least one folder existed and none was the project. A path on a drive that does not exist (an unmapped letter, or a share that is unplugged or unreachable) proves nothing and answers false. That also stops a later subst or net use from turning a kept entry into the project.
- A project that went missing makes every call throw NoSuchFileException, so the answer is false.
- Cost is O(depth) calls, each opening two handles. No cache and no new state.
Its KDoc gives the why: on Windows, toRealPath calls GetFinalPathNameByHandle only at a reparse point, so a subst or mapped drive letter is never resolved. `Q:\bin` can then be `<project>\bin` with no shared prefix, and only identity sees it. Node's realpath.native resolves these, so VS Code needs no twin.

(b) isOutsideProject:
- After the existing checks (absolute; plain-local spelling first; every form plain local and not within the project) pass, add on a Windows host only (`windowsHost`): `val project = realPathOrNull(basePath)`, then `project != null && outsideByIdentity(realForm ?: candidate.normalize(), project)`.
- realForm is the value the `resolve` seam returned, so compute it once and reuse it.
- Identity runs only for entries that would otherwise be kept.
- POSIX does not change: no identity walk there.
- Keep both outer catches.
- KDoc: add 'and, on a Windows host, no existing folder from it up to its root is the project (file identity)'.

(c) select: add a when-branch before `else`: `windowsHost && !outsideByIdentity(real, project) -> rejected("$label resolves inside the project", real)`.
- `project` there is already the real path.
- The reason string is the existing one, which is also what VS Code reports for the same subst case.
- An identity lookup failure is practically unreachable for a path toRealPath just resolved, and it refuses the same way (fail closed). Say so in a comment.
- This covers installedExecutable (node) and installedArtifact (daemon, wrapper, proxy).

No other production file changes. protectedPathEntries, nodeOnProtectedPath, protectedDaemonEnvironment, protectedDaemonCommand, TerminalAgentLauncher, ManagedVmPanel:137-138 and ProtectedStateStore.usableFor inherit the change with unchanged signatures. LEGACY never calls them.

  This is the Windows equivalent of `cd moe-jetbrains && ./gradlew test`. Run it from a /mnt/d cwd.
